title: Pendulum

caveats: Some frames show a semi-transparent duplicate/ghost of the ball and string that can confuse tracking.

reference.basis: Striped pole has no stated length and is not a standard size.

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion; motion appears as real-time animation.

subjects.description: small red spherical bob hanging from a thin black string from an overhead mount

observation.what_happens: A red ball suspended by a thin string swings side to side beneath a fixed horizontal mount. It begins displaced to the right, swings left through the vertical, and is still oscillating when the clip ends.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: Path fits a circle to 0.07 px and theta is only +/-0.14 rad (~8 deg) with slow decay from 0.14 to 0.12 over 6.45 s and period ~1.5 s, so it is a near-harmonic pendulum where g is fixed and L comes from frequency. Candidates go from textbook undamped small-angle to sine-pendulum with linear viscous damping to sine-pendulum with quadratic air drag to test which loss law extrapolates best.

critique.finding: The ball swings as a pendulum with length {L} slowed by air pushing harder at higher speed with strength {cq}.
critique.headline: Air drag that grows with speed shapes the swing
critique.why_it_won: The winner keeps the swing size right to the end because its drag strengthens at high speed, while steady friction lets the size drift off.

headline: Air drag that grows with speed shapes the swing
finding: The ball swings as a pendulum with length 0.6 ± 4.91e-5 m slowed by air pushing harder at higher speed with strength 0.107 ± 7.69e-4 dimensionless.

eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle pendulum period T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) gives L from measured period, with quadratic air drag force ~ v|v| giving angular equation theta'' + (g/L)*sin(theta) + cq*theta'|theta'| = 0, so peak amplitude decays as 1/theta_max(t) = 1/theta0 + (4*cq*omega0/3*pi)*t.
